Australian Imaging Biomarkers and Lifestyle (AIBL) Study of Ageing
Eli Lilly and Company
institutions.sourceScope: Cogstate named Lilly preferred provider for AD trial cognitive endpoint quality (2017), also Bio-Hermes study participant; terms/fees not disclosed.

institutions.name: Biogen Inc.
institutions.sourceScope: Project Intuition with Cambridge Cognition used repeated device-based remote cognitive tests, around 23k participants; study participation does not prove KIMSE demand.

institutions.name: Merck & Co., Inc. (MSD)
institutions.sourceScope: 2021 direct Evidation collaboration to study passive smartphone/wearable endpoints for Alzheimer disease; spend and Korean-cohort interest undisclosed.

institutions.name: Evidation
institutions.sourceScope: Evidation's named 2021 Merck Alzheimer's remote digital monitoring partnership establishes platform/operational precedent, not Evidation willingness to resell Korean data.

institutions.name: IQVIA Real World Solutions
institutions.sourceScope: Official evidence networks and Analytics Research Accelerator describe global data providers, patient registries, dataset curation and licensing; no KIMSE relationship.

institutions.name: Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine
institutions.sourceScope: ki:elements lists ReTain Phase 2b AD collaboration with Johnson & Johnson; contract amount, Korean cohort demand and payment terms unverified.

institutions.name: Linus Health
institutions.sourceScope: Named by GAP as Bio-Hermes-002 technology/study partner, not proven buyer of external cohorts.

institutions.name: Shionogi & Co., Ltd.
institutions.sourceScope: Feb 2026 Cumulus Neuroscience announced Shionogi as new Japan customer using NeuLogiq for S-898270; study indication not shown to be AD-specific.

institutions.name: National Center for Geriatrics and Gerontology (NCGG)
institutions.sourceScope: Operates NILS-LSA longitudinal epidemiology and dementia biobank with ethics/data access governance; not a purchaser of KIMSE data.

institutions.name: Fujirebio
institutions.sourceScope: Fujirebio named Bio-Hermes-002 study biomarker partner; product/assay validation role does not establish cohort purchasing.

institutions.name: Korea National Institute of Health — BRIDGE
institutions.sourceScope: KDCA BRIDGE programme operates early-onset/late-onset dementia and community high-risk cohorts with standardized clinical and imaging data; not a direct KIMSE customer.

institutions.name: Korea Dementia Research and Development Center (KDRC)
institutions.sourceScope: SNU's Jan 2026 release says standardized common dementia dataset and samples from 1,765 people across 29 hospitals, for research distribution; no KIMSE agreement.

institutions.name: German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE)
institutions.sourceScope: DZNE DELCODE long-term observational AD/SCD/MCI study and PROSPECT-AD speech validation; not an identified external Korean cohort purchaser.

institutions.name: ki:elements
institutions.sourceScope: Lists PROSPECT-AD with DZNE and ReTain with J&J among digital speech cognition assessment research; no KIMSE relation.

institutions.name: Amsterdam UMC / Amsterdam Dementia Cohort
institutions.sourceScope: Official ADC describes almost 7,000 consenting clinical patients, comprehensive assessment and annual follow-up; does not evidence willingness to buy Korean smartphone data.

institutions.name: Roche / Genentech
institutions.sourceScope: GAP Feb 2025 announced Roche collaboration in Bio-Hermes-002 biomarker platform; financing/rights differ from direct digital feature purchase.

institutions.name: Sanofi
institutions.sourceScope: May 2026 GAP announcement Sanofi joins Bio-Hermes-002 as collaboration partner; no evidence of specific paid Korean cohort order.

institutions.name: UNSW Centre for Healthy Brain Ageing — Sydney Memory and Ageing Study
institutions.sourceScope: Official longitudinal MAS from 2005, >1,000 baseline subjects; research data access via DPAU and application fees; fees are access charges, not KIMSE vendor demand.

institutions.name: Swedish BioFINDER / Lund University
institutions.sourceScope: Swedish BioFINDER prospectively observes cognitively healthy, SCD/MCI and dementia cohorts; repeated cognitive/clinical assessments and biomarkers. Research cohort, not KIMSE buyer.

institutions.name: Barcelonaβeta Brain Research Center / ALFA10
institutions.sourceScope: ALFA10 extends ALFA longitudinal preclinical Alzheimer research and describes digital and remote cognitive/other change monitoring. No external Korean dataset purchase indicated.

institutions.name: University of Eastern Finland / FINGER study
institutions.sourceScope: Official UEF FINGER project 1,259 older adults, 2-year multidomain lifestyle intervention, later 5/7/11-year follow-ups. Trial is not a paid KIMSE cohort purchase.

institutions.name: Trinity College Dublin / TILDA
institutions.sourceScope: National longitudinal aging study with repeated neurocognitive research and official data access procedure. Cognitive aging study, not proof of a data-purchasing programme.

institutions.name: LASI-DAD / AIIMS New Delhi research collaboration
institutions.sourceScope: LASI-DAD national dementia assessment survey uses repeated cognition, informant interviews and biological measurements; wave 2 dataset available in 2026. Co-led by USC and AIIMS India, country assigned by field cohort.

institutions.name: Policlinico Gemelli / INTERCEPTOR
institutions.sourceScope: Italian Ministry of Health and AIFA funded INTERCEPTOR for MCI-to-Alzheimer progression biomarkers; older project, current activity not confirmed.

institutions.name: National Neuroscience Institute / NNRC Dementia
institutions.sourceScope: NNI dementia research platform explicitly lists longitudinal observational studies, clinical trials, neuropsychological assessments, fluid biomarkers and neuroimaging.

institutions.name: Taiwan ADNI / Chang Gung Memorial Hospital research
institutions.sourceScope: Taiwan ADNI official project documents follow-up correlating clinical, biological and neuroimaging markers for MCI/AD; no commercial purchase evidence.

institutions.name: Danish Dementia Research Centre / Rigshospitalet
institutions.sourceScope: Copenhagen Memory Clinic affiliated DDRC reports 1,500–2,000 referrals per year, clinical research and an AD clinical trials unit, not proven data purchasing.

institutions.name: NTNU / HUNT4 70+ study
institutions.sourceScope: NTNU HUNT4 70+ examines dementia and aging with gait/physical and cognitive assessments, biomarker follow-up; study lead profile confirms subsequent planned HUNT5.

institutions.name: Fiocruz / UFMG ELSI-Brazil
institutions.sourceScope: ELSI-Brazil is national aging survey with 2015–16, 2019–21 and 2023–24 waves. Official portal warns cross-sectional wave files cannot be simply joined for longitudinal analysis.

institutions.name: Mexican Health and Aging Study / Mex-Cog
institutions.sourceScope: MHAS national 50+ longitudinal cohort, with Mex-Cog ancillary HCAP deep cognitive assessment and informant reports. Multi-institution programme, not paid KIMSE buyer.

institutions.name: University of the Witwatersrand / HAALSI Dementia
institutions.sourceScope: Wits/Harvard HAALSI long-term aging/cognitive and dementia study with cognitive assessments, informant and biomarker measures, and new research waves. No Korean data buying shown.

institutions.name: University of Auckland / Dementia Prevention Research Clinic
institutions.sourceScope: Auckland dementia prevention clinic follows MCI and very early AD participants longitudinally with lifestyle, family input, blood and brain imaging. Published general research clinic email dprc@uoa.auckland.ac.nz.

masterPolicy: ISO 3166-1 249 official country/territory codes are planned-screening master only, not all researched. Institution records currently cover 24 geographically assigned codes.
authorityScale: KIMSE internal contextual research-influence band A/B/C, determined from published institutional type and research evidence only. Not an independent ranking, endorsement, scientific validity grade, or partnership validation.
